_comment: Packages whose own tests provision real ephemeral infrastructure (Docker containers via testcontainers-go, or multi-process real-time distributed coordination), so a test failure inside one of them is, per FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #61, at least as likely to be local resource contention as a real defect: 'the specific package that loses the race changes between runs... is the signature of resource contention, not a code defect.' tools/testgate (the local pre-push gate; see .githooks/pre-push and the Makefile's push-gate target) downgrades a test failure confined to a package listed here to a warning rather than blocking the push. GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/ci.yml) is unaffected because it runs no tests at all: it runs `make ci-remote` (build, vet, fmt, tidy, the two pinned scanners, the docs and chart checks), so nothing in this file changes what that workflow accepts. What it does change is the local run, and the local run is now the only place a test result comes from at all: `make ci` still uses the bare, non-tolerant test-race/test-integration targets and hard-fails on a listed package exactly like an unlisted one, while `make push-gate` downgrades it to a warning. An entry added here without a real, written reason is therefore a package that nothing anywhere checks. Every entry names one package by its full import path and a reason grepped/derived from real evidence (a specific test, a specific failure shape, or CLAUDE.md's own list of Docker-dependent packages), never a directory glob or 'seems container-ish' guess. A package that stops provisioning real infrastructure should be removed from this list in the same change that removes the infrastructure, the same staleness discipline gosec-waivers.json's own header asks for. TAXONOMY ADDED 2026-09-15, and it exists to stop a future reader overreacting to a red package name. Nine packages failed the push-gate run that landed tools/sweep, and they are not one phenomenon: seven were HARNESS-ONLY (the failure is in provisioning, before any assertion runs), one was REAL TIMING TEST DEADLINE ONLY (internal/event's deliberate severance chaos test, whose window is the test's own and has no production counterpart), and one was REAL TIMING PRODUCTION RELEVANT (internal/election, whose 2-second fencing-token-less lease behaves the same way under a production GC pause as under test starvation). Those nine entries now open with a CLASS: line saying which. An entry with no CLASS: line has simply not been classified yet; that is an absence of work, not a third category, and the same rule the cmd/runner entry states applies to it: a reader cannot tell a prediction from a record, so do not infer one.

packages.reason: FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #61 names TestGrandIntegration specifically as a repeat offender under full parallel `-race` load. Confirmed again in the AWX_PARITY_ROADMAP.md 3b.1 session (2026-08-12/13): TestGrandIntegration_EachKindReachesItsOwnAdapter hung 913s behind a device-lock-contention redelivery loop, and a later run failed a different test, TestGrandIntegration, on a NATS container port-mapping race ('port "4222/tcp" not found'). Both reproduced as clean, fast passes every time when rerun in isolation, and a git-stash baseline comparison proved the first failure was not reachable from that session's own diff at all. NARROWED 2026-09-16, and the narrowing is the entry's whole point now. This entry covered the package, so it tolerated every test in it, and that hid a total regression for a full session: every job in the system hung in "running" forever (FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #222), four tests here failed on it in five consecutive push-gate runs, and every run printed "passed (warnings above)". The two tests above were the ones this entry's own prose had always named; TestCredentialInjection_ReachesARealPlaybookThroughTheRealBinaries and TestChaos_NATSSeverance were never observed to flake and are deliberately NOT listed, so a failure in either is hard. TestChaos_PostgresSeverance USED to be listed here, and was removed on 2026-09-23 because the harness defect this entry named was fixed rather than tolerated: startChaosHarness's postgres and toxiproxy starts inherited testcontainers' hardcoded sixty second readiness deadline (WithAdditionalWaitStrategy and WithWaitStrategy both build ForAll(...).WithDeadline(60s)), while every NATS start waited two minutes. Every postgres and toxiproxy start in the repository now waits under testsupport.ContainerStartupTimeout through testsupport.PostgresReady and ToxiproxyReady, and testsupport's TestNoContainerWaitsUnderTheLibraryDeadline fails if any reverts. A failure in that test is therefore hard again.

CLASS: REAL TIMING, TEST DEADLINE ONLY (classified 2026-09-15). Unlike the harness-only entries, the flake here is in a real mechanism rather than in provisioning: TestNatsBus_SurvivesConnectionSeverance severs a real broker on a real container network and asserts recovery inside a window, so CPU starvation under full-suite load can push the reconnect past that window. It is still not a production signal, because the window is the test's own deadline and production has none: a slow reconnect there is slowness, not incorrectness. This test is deliberately timing-sensitive and cannot be made fast, so it is expected to stay on this list. ORIGINAL ENTRY: FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #61 names TestNatsBus_SurvivesConnectionSeverance and TestNatsBusPublish_DistinctEventsBothStored as failing under full-suite parallel load and passing individually every time. Dials a real, ephemeral NATS container per CLAUDE.md's own list of Docker-dependent packages.

CLASS: HARNESS-ONLY (classified 2026-09-15 against the push-gate run that landed tools/sweep). The observed failure is in test-infrastructure provisioning, before any assertion in this package runs. A failure here is evidence about the Docker daemon or about testcontainers losing a race under parallel load, NOT evidence of a defect in this package and NOT evidence of instability in production, where neither testcontainers nor a four-pass suite exists. Do not escalate one. Reclassified 2026-09-15 from the middle class to this one after reading the named test. TestNewNatsLockManagerRejectsOldServer starts a nats:2.10 container and asserts that NewNatsLockManager refuses it. Neither load nor timing can turn that assertion false: the only load-sensitive step is the container start, which t.Fatalf's on its own line. So the flake is provisioning, like the six above. Worth knowing separately, and NOT the flake: the assertion is only err != nil, so a connection failure would pass this test for the wrong reason. ORIGINAL ENTRY: FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #61 names TestNewNatsLockManagerRejectsOldServer as failing under full-suite parallel load and passing individually every time. Starts up to seven real containers in a single package (the Makefile's own GO_TEST_TIMEOUT comment), the heaviest real-infrastructure user in the module.

CLAUDE.md's own list of packages that dial real ephemeral Docker containers (NATS, sshd) names this one alongside internal/lock and internal/event; genuinely container-dependent by the identical mechanism, and excluding it while including its two named siblings would be an arbitrary distinction. OBSERVED DIRECTLY 2026-08-16, which is the correction that matters: this entry used to say 'not yet observed to flake directly', and it was admitted on the strength of the mechanism alone. It has now been seen in two consecutive full `make ci` runs, with the same signature both times, `failed to get mapped port: port "2222/tcp" not found` raised by TestSSHContainer_StoppedContainerRetriesThenBreakerOpens and by the shared-container setup TestSSHContainer_ExecSuccess and its three siblings use. The mechanism is precise rather than general: the openssh-server container starts, satisfies its wait.ForLog("done.") strategy, and has lost its published port binding by the time the very next statement asks for it, which is what a container that has exited looks like to an inspect. Under full parallel -race load that test took 18.31s; run alone immediately afterwards, against the same daemon and the same image, it passed in 9.35s. The goleak failures that accompany it in the same runs are downstream rather than separate: a setup that t.Fatal's skips the terminate that would stop the testcontainers reaper, so the leaked goroutine is a consequence of the port failure and not an independent defect.

CLASS: REAL TIMING, PRODUCTION RELEVANT (classified 2026-09-15). This is the ONE entry on this list that says something true about production. The lease is 2 seconds with no fencing token (internal/election's electionTTL), so a holder that fails to renew while still believing it leads is a real outcome, reached in test by parallel-load starvation and in production by a GC pause, a throttled CPU or a paused VM. It is not a latent bug: every consumer of IsLeader is already safe under two simultaneous leaders (the scheduler by the unique index on schedule_occurrence, the fan-out reaper by publishing under an idempotency key inside the stream's duplicate window, session sweeping by being naturally idempotent). Read a failure here as a prompt to check that a NEW consumer carries its own guard, not as a prompt to panic. ORIGINAL ENTRY: AWX_PARITY_ROADMAP.md 3b.1 session (2026-08-13): TestLeaderElection_ThreeReplicas_OnlyOneLeaderAndGracefulHandover failed under full-suite parallel load (a real three-replica timing race against a real NATS-backed lease, the same mechanism cmd/controller's own leader-election gate exercises one layer up), confirmed passing individually afterward.

OBSERVED DIRECTLY 2026-08-16, on the same day and for the same reason as internal/transport/ssh's entry above: this one used to say 'not yet observed to flake in a full-suite run', and TestSSHMeshReleaseGate_RealSecretThroughTheFullChain then failed under a full `make push-gate` and passed on a rerun. Both entries were admitted on mechanism alone and both were right about the mechanism, which is the argument for prophylactic listing and also the reason a 'not yet observed' clause has to be revisited rather than left to age into an unexamined fact: a reader six months from now cannot tell a prediction from a record, and the whole value of this file is that every entry is a record.

Not a defect in the test: the failure is inside the shared broker-start helper before any assertion runs. Reran the package alone immediately afterwards and it passed in 26.9s, which is the isolation signature FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #61 describes. The package provisions two real ephemeral nats:2.14.4-alpine containers, one per Release Gate, and both run a JetStream-enabled broker in operator mode, so it belongs on this list for the same mechanism as internal/event and internal/lock.

Observed 2026-08-26 in the same push-gate run as internal/meshid above: TestReleaseGate_AnInputResolvesOutOfARealVault failed with 'container port: port "8200/tcp" not found'. Same race, different image: the port mapping is not published yet when the test reads it, under full parallel repeat load. Reran alone immediately afterwards and it passed in 12.9s. The package provisions a real ephemeral HashiCorp Vault container. That two different packages lost the same race in one run, on two different ports, is itself FAILURE_PATTERNS.md #61's stated signature: 'the specific package that loses the race changes between runs'.

Observed 2026-08-26 under `make push-gate`'s test-repeat: TestConformance_LeavesNoGoroutinesBehind failed with 'found unexpected goroutines', and the goroutine it named was testcontainers' OWN reaper connection (testcontainers-go@v0.43.0/reaper.go:544-549), not anything pkg/netconf starts. The reaper connects lazily and its goroutine can still be live when a later package's goleak check runs, so whether this fires depends on which package happens to be last to touch the shared reaper. Reran the test alone immediately afterwards and it passed in 12.6s. The package provisions a real ephemeral netopeer2 NETCONF container, which is the same criterion every other entry here meets. This is a leak-detector reporting a dependency's own goroutine, not a leak in this repository's code, so it is listed rather than chased.

ORIGINAL ENTRY: Observed 2026-08-26 under `make push-gate`, and the evidence is unusually clean because the package PASSED TWICE in the same run before failing: ok at test-race and ok at test-repeat, then FAIL inside push-gate-coverage, which is the fourth full suite pass of one invocation. Same commit, same code, same machine. The four tests named were TestConnect_Succeeds, TestConnect_UnreachableEndpoint, TestDiscover_YieldsAccountThenInstances and TestSync_RoundTripsRealInstances, and the failure is not in any of them: it is 'shared LocalStack container setup failed: ... wait until ready: get state: Get http://%2Fvar%2Frun%2Fdocker.sock/... context deadline exceeded', which is the Docker daemon failing to answer a state query, not an assertion. The package provisions a real ephemeral LocalStack container, the heaviest single container this repository starts, so it is the first to lose when the daemon is saturated late in a multi-pass run.

Observed 2026-08-26 under `make push-gate`, with the same signature as this file's internal/inventory/plugins/aws entry and the same single root cause: the package passed EARLIER IN THE SAME INVOCATION and failed on a later pass. ok at test-race, FAIL at test-integration, in one push-gate run. Every one of its tests failed together, which is the shape of a shared container that never came up rather than of a defect, and the underlying error is the Docker daemon timing out on a state query while starting LocalStack. This package, internal/catalog/cloud/aws/ec2 and internal/inventory/plugins/aws are the three LocalStack consumers in this repository; they fail together, for one reason, and are listed together so a future reader does not diagnose them separately. All three were already in the Makefile's DOCKER_DEPENDENT_PACKAGES.

Observed 2026-08-26 under `make push-gate`, and the evidence here is the sharpest of the LocalStack group: this package holds the SHARED sync-plugin conformance suite, which drives every registered plugin through the identical assertions, and when it failed, every single failing subtest was the /aws one. TestPluginConformance_CloseIsSafe/aws, DiscoverStreamsUnclassifiedRecords/aws, ForeignOwnerIsAConflict/aws, ReadOnlyInventoryIsADryRun/aws, ResyncIsIdempotent/aws and SyncOnboardsEveryDevice/aws all failed while the same six assertions passed for every other plugin in the same run. That is not a conformance defect, which would fail across plugins; it is the LocalStack container this file already records for internal/inventory/plugins/aws, reached through the conformance suite. This is the fourth and last LocalStack consumer in the repository. Already in DOCKER_DEPENDENT_PACKAGES.
